name: Midjourney
tagline: Text-to-image generation service known for high-quality aesthetic output

pricing.notes: Official docs checked 2026-07-30; Basic is $10/month, Standard $30, Pro $60, Mega $120.

verdictSummary: You can build a wrapper around open models, but you cannot solo-recreate Midjourney's proprietary model quality, style tuning, infrastructure, and community distribution.
coreLoopDIY: Use Stable Diffusion/Flux-style local or hosted models with a prompt UI and gallery.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for the model and taste layer, not the chat box around it.

priorArt.name: ComfyUI
priorArt.desc: Open-source node-based UI for running image-generation workflows locally or on a GPU serve

notes: Must-have no: one of the clearest frontier-model moat cases.
prompt:
Honest answer: don't try to rebuild Midjourney. The product is a proprietary
frontier model plus years of aesthetic tuning, and no wrapper written in a weekend
gets you that output. What you can build is a private studio around open models.

Build me a local image-generation studio wrapping open models. Requirements:

- A local web app (Node + Express, plain HTML/JS) on localhost:4890: prompt box,
  generate-4 button, gallery grid of results.
- Backend targets whichever engine I have: a local ComfyUI instance running Flux or
  SDXL if there is a GPU, otherwise a hosted API like Replicate or fal.ai (key in
  .env). Same UI either way.
- Every image saved to ~/ImageGen/YYYY-MM/ with a sidecar JSON: prompt, seed,
  model, steps, so any result is reproducible later.
- Gallery with search over past prompts (SQLite FTS5), favorites, and one-click
  re-run with the same seed or a new variation.
- Style presets in a styles.json of prompt prefixes and suffixes I can toggle, a
  poor man's style reference.
- Everything local except hosted-API calls. No accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: training or fine-tuning models, and matching Midjourney's look.
  This trades the taste layer for control and privacy, say so in the README.
- README: both engine setups and the rough cost per image on the hosted route.
